title: Six untied transformer blocks at full width (d_model 256) instead of five (4.79M parameters)
description: Depth follow-up to 051-claude (no backlog ID; closest are the P24/P25 capacity-allocation entries): N_LAYER 5 -> 6 at unchanged width, heads, d_ff, Muon/AdamW optimizer and schedule, separating depth from the width cut that 057-claude (six blocks at d_model 224, 277) confounded it with. One more sequential attention+MLP application per token should let the pretrained model compose one more inference/citation step internally, which is what expert iteration needs to extend 6-line pretraining proofs to the >=7-line dev-transfer targets.
hypothesis: The 4 -> 5 block change (043 275 -> 051 286) helped via sequential depth, not parameters: a sixth full-width block adds another residual update per token for multi-hop citation lookups (find the premise lines, then the rule that combines them), making round-1/2 RL sample accuracy on longer targets higher, so expert iteration harvests more >=7-line proofs. 057 did not refute this because it removed 12.5% of the width to hold parameters fixed. The cost is ~16% fewer pretraining steps in the fixed 300 s, which matters little because 5-layer pretraining is near-saturated (val loss ~0.059, held-out greedy 0.988), and slower decode is fixed-sample, so it only costs wall-clock inside the 1200 s cap.
expected_delta: -20 to +20 dev-transfer solves at >=7 versus 286 (central estimate +5); a timeout on any seed is the main failure mode (predicted total ~1090-1140 s)

arch.change: one knob: N_LAYER 5 -> 6 in pretrain.py; d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout and every other setting unchanged
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=6 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.5
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (6 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 24 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 6 blocks) are in Muon. Six qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction with 6 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 24 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of six blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0. No reinitialization during RL. The sixth block consumes extra global-RNG draws during construction, so random initial weights are not bitwise identical to 051's for a given seed; the init rule is identical.
config.timing: Not benchmarked locally for this run. Expectation from records: 051 (5 x 256) ran 2320-2370 pretraining steps, total 1053 s; 057 (6 x 224) ran ~2187 steps, total 1089 s with RL sampling 558-616 samples/s, so decode is dominated by per-layer overhead. Predict ~1950-2050 pretraining steps (FLOPs per token +20%) and total ~1090-1140 s, under TOTAL_SECS 1200.
